newsitem.title: FRANCE: Trichet says Maastricht criteria must be respected.
newsitem.headline: Trichet says Maastricht criteria must be respected.

text.p: Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Wednesday it was not in the interests of any country to join a single European currency before its economy had fully converged.
In a radio interview, he repeated that Maastricht treaty convergence criteria for joining a single currency in January 1999 must be respected.
"It is not in the interests of any country which has not sufficiently converged to join," he said.
He had been asked about a French opposition Socialist party demand that Italy join the single currency from the start.
Trichet said he hoped as many countries as possible would join the new euro in 1999 and declined to comment on the membership chances of any one individual country.

Trichet also reiterated that he believed Germany was determined to meet Maastricht treaty criteria in 1997, the key year for deciding which countries qualify to join a single currency when it is first launched. (( -- Paris Newsroom +33 1 42 21 53 81))
